title: K-flat invertibility of the cochain localization tensorator
statement: For a commutative ring A and a scheme T, the native cochain localization tensorator mu of QA from cochain sheaves of A-modules on the pro-etale site of T to their derived category is invertible whenever its right input is K-flat. Use the native derived tensor structure [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] and fixed sheaf coefficient categories [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data]. Write the actual native localization tensorator with its explicit source and target as cochainLocalizationTensor, then state invertibility of this same map; no map is changed.

source.place: Step 2: finite reduction is derived scalar tensor and its compatibility with invertible twists follows from derived tensor associativity; Stacks Tags 07A4 and 0FPT.

proof.text: Write the actual native localization tensorator as cochainLocalizationTensor with its explicit morphism type. For its invertibility, pass K-flatness through the quotient into the homotopy category. The native Qh tensor counit is invertible with K-flat right input. Q is the monoidal transport of the composite of the strong monoidal quotient and Qh. Its tensorator is therefore a composite of functorial isomorphisms and that invertible Qh tensorator. The generic argument is a proved private helper; the public theorem gives the concrete sheaf instance for the explicitly typed same map.

proof_origin: J2, 2026-10-26: expose this proved native property as a public named API because the actual certified scalar diagram definition must refer to named proved theorems, not private proof helpers. No sorry is introduced. The public API is specialized to actual sheaf module categories; the generic localization argument is a proved private helper. This avoids repeating the expensive concrete monoidal-instance specialization inside every data constructor. Its native tensorator has an explicit typed map definition, shared by the diagram constructor and this property theorem, to avoid expansion of the lax-monoidal instance merely to compare map types.
